scope: Correction to the seam coverage guard after full-suite regression; wider M2 and native gates remain open
failure: The first full suite failed the original-scan Float32 face-crossing control because the seam area-vector difference was 8.825445547699928e-7 against a reference magnitude of 0.0018825459479558952, approximately 0.047% relative. The original machine-epsilon-only threshold rejected this existing supported helper case.
change: Seam materialization allows a relative area-vector difference of 1e-9 for precise output and 1e-3 for its internal Float32 output, in addition to its machine-arithmetic bound. The separate precise assembly projected-area guard is unchanged. Both known material-loss controls still reject.
preview: The revised seam source was copied to the 5173 combined preview after its previous content matched the recorded baseline; its served module contains the guard and Float32 allowance.
limitations: The tolerances are explicit loss allowances, not exact coverage or native-equivalence guarantees.
The 1e-3 Float32 allowance is supported by the current real-face control but has not been established as a universal geometry-quality threshold.
The ten expected failures represent known native Split comparisons, not native parity; the previous passing typecheck predates this small numeric adjustment.
Native Split mismatches and the other M2 acceptance gates remain open.
